title: "A common grade report for two scores"
subtitle: "4.3 · on the postrank package's six fictional sites"
description: "Weighted directional errors and criterion-specific profiles of a common report."
---

One grade report ranks all six sites together. Wrong directions carry weight $w$ on score A and $1-w$ on score B; withholding a pair costs $\tau$ once.


## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Equal weights.** States 9 pairs at risk .0933, with wrong shares .0177 on score A and .0267 on score B.
- **No cap.** Searching all 4,683 reports keeps the same 9 stated pairs because grades must stay coherent.
- **A-heavy.** Restores {A, B} > {C, D} > {E, F}, stating 12 pairs.
- **Score A only.** Follows score A between blocks, leaving a .237 wrong share on score B.
- **w .70.** Keeps {B, C, D} together, with a .115 wrong share on score B.
- **Score B only.** The best report is tied with another report, with score A wrong shares .200 and .215.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
two <- postrank(pr_tutorial$two, weights = c(score_A=.5, score_B=.5), tau=.2, G_max=3L, backend="highs")
get_grades(two); get_profile(two)[c("criterion", "E_over_N", "risk")]
```
:::

<details>
<summary>Model notes</summary>

The example uses independent normal posteriors. Grade one has highest priority, and pairs in the same grade are left unranked. The error bound applies to the expected average across stated pairs; individual directions can have higher error probabilities. Each weight setting defines the loss used to choose and evaluate the report.

</details>

Standalone: [two-scores](../../embed/two-scores.html), for example `?w=.5&tau=.2&cap=all`.

Related applications: [Reporting risk and withholding cost](../grades/price-of-silence.qmd).
